title: Go: Feature Flags
description: Build a feature flag system with boolean flags, percentage rollouts, user targeting, multi-variant A/B testing, and an evaluation pipeline.

steps.title: Flag struct and boolean isEnabled
steps.description: Define a `Flag` struct with `Key string`, `Enabled bool`, and `Description string`. Create a `FlagManager` with `map[string]*Flag`. Implement `AddFlag(f *Flag)` and `IsEnabled(key string) bool`. Print whether a flag named `"new-checkout"` is enabled via `fmt.Println(fm.IsEnabled("new-checkout"))`.
hints: `IsEnabled` returns the `Enabled` field if the flag exists.
Return `false` if the flag key is not found.

verification.failureMessage: IsEnabled should return the flag's Enabled value.

steps.title: Percentage rollout using hash
steps.description: Add `RolloutPercentage int` (0-100) to `Flag`. Implement `IsEnabledForUser(key, userID string) bool` that uses a consistent hash (e.g. `hash(userID + key) % 100 < RolloutPercentage`) to determine if the flag is enabled for that user. Print results for multiple user IDs with a 50% rollout.
hints: Same user ID consistently gets the same result.

verification.successMessage: Percentage rollout works with consistent hashing.
verification.failureMessage: Same userID should always get the same result for a given flag.

steps.title: User attribute targeting
steps.description: Add `TargetingRules []TargetingRule` to `Flag`. Each `TargetingRule` has `Attribute string`, `Operator string` (`"equals"`, `"contains"`, `"in"`), and `Values []string`. `IsEnabledFor(key string, user map[string]string)` evaluates rules against user attributes. Print the result for a user with `{"country": "US"}` and a rule `country equals US`.
hints: Iterate rules; if any rule matches, return the flag's enabled for that user.
Use `user[rule.Attribute]` to get the attribute value.
For `"in"` operator, check if the value is in `rule.Values`.

verification.failureMessage: A user with country=US should match a rule country equals US.

steps.title: Multi-variant A/B testing
steps.description: Add `Variants []Variant` to `Flag` where `Variant` has `Name string` and `Weight int` (percentage). Implement `GetVariant(key, userID string) (string, error)` that returns a variant based on weighted random assignment (consistent hash). Print the variant name for a given user.
hints: Total weights should sum to 100 (validate on add).
Hash userID+key to get a number 0-99, then iterate variants accumulating weight.
Return the variant where the hash falls in its weight range.

verification.successMessage: Multi-variant A/B test returns a variant.
verification.failureMessage: GetVariant should return one of the defined variants consistently.

steps.title: User overrides
steps.description: Add `UserOverrides map[string]bool` (userID → enabled) and `VariantOverrides map[string]string` (userID → variantName) to `Flag`. Override evaluation takes priority over all other logic. Print the result for an overridden user vs a non-overridden user.
hints: Check overrides first in `IsEnabledForUser` before applying any other logic.
Use `ok` pattern: `if val, ok := f.UserOverrides[userID]; ok { return val }`.

verification.successMessage: User overrides take priority over other evaluation.
verification.failureMessage: An overridden user should always get the override value.

steps.title: Evaluation pipeline
steps.description: Implement a `Evaluate(key string, user User) Evaluation` pipeline that runs all steps in order: (1) overrides, (2) targeting rules, (3) percentage rollout, (4) default enabled. `Evaluation` has `Key, Variant string` and `Reason string`. Print the evaluation result for a complex scenario with all layers.
hints: Define `User` struct with `ID string` and `Attributes map[string]string`.
Pipeline short-circuits at the first match.
`Reason` explains which step determined the result (e.g. `"override"`, `"targeting"`, `"rollout"`, `"default"`).

verification.successMessage: Evaluation pipeline runs all steps in order.
verification.failureMessage: Evaluation should include the reason for the flag's state.
